contentMarkdown:
# Keyboard Accessibility & Focus Management

Keyboard accessibility lets people navigate and operate an interface through a keyboard interface. Focus management determines which element receives keyboard input as people move through the page, open a dialog, or return to their task.

## What should you test?

| Check | What to look for |
|---|---|
| **Keyboard operation and exit (2.1.1 and 2.1.2, A)** | Reach and use controls without a mouse. Follow the expected keys for each widget. Make sure users can leave any component they enter. |
| **Focus order (2.4.3, A)** | When navigating sequentially, focus follows an order that preserves meaning and operation. Start from a logical document order. |
| **Visible focus (2.4.7, AA)** | The user can see which control currently has keyboard focus. Check default and custom focus styles. |
| **Focus not obscured** | Under WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.4.11 (AA), content created by the site must leave at least part of the focused component visible. Test sticky headers, bottom bars, and overlays while tabbing. |

## Example: A booking-change dialog

1. Tab to the **Change booking** button and activate it. Focus moves inside the modal to a sensible starting point, such as the heading for a long dialog or the safer action for a hard-to-reverse change.
2. Use **Tab** and **Shift+Tab** to move between controls. Sequential focus stays inside the open modal. Check that the dialog’s sticky footer does not cover focused controls in the scrolling content.
3. Press **Escape** or use the visible close control. Focus normally returns to **Change booking**. If the trigger no longer exists or the user’s action leads to a different logical location, move focus to an appropriate element in that flow.

A modal can keep focus inside while it is open and still provide a keyboard way out. The modal pattern depends on a working exit and sensible focus placement after closing.

## Where should teams start?

Use native buttons and links for common actions and navigation. For a custom widget, confirm its expected keyboard interaction and test it in context. Check focus return in the product as well as the component preview. In the product, the trigger might disappear when the booking changes.

name: Figma Code Connect
definition: Figma Code Connect links components in a Figma design library to their implementations in a codebase. Those connections help developers and AI agents find the real code associated with a design component.
sources: Getting started with Code Connect CLI, Figma (https://developers.figma.com/docs/code-connect/quickstart-guide/)
contentMarkdown:
# Figma Code Connect

Figma Code Connect links components in a Figma design library to their implementations in a codebase. Those connections help developers and AI agents find the real code associated with a design component.

## What does Code Connect add?

A design component and a code component can have different names, property values, and composition rules. A connection records how the two relate, rather than asking someone to infer the implementation from appearance.

For example, a Figma button might have a Size value of Large, while the code API accepts `size="large"`. Mapping that relationship makes the intended implementation easier to retrieve.

A connection is a reference to implementation knowledge. It does not prove that every screen using the component behaves correctly.

## Code Connect UI vs. CLI

Figma provides a UI for connecting design components to repository implementations and a CLI for publishing connections and code examples. The CLI's recommended template approach lets teams control the snippets and property mappings they expose.

The interfaces have different editing and configuration workflows. Check Figma's current comparison and access requirements before choosing one. Avoid assuming that every connection method produces the same Dev Mode snippet experience.

## How does it relate to the Figma MCP server?

The [Figma MCP server](/glossary/figma-mcp-server.html) supplies design context to a connected agent. Code Connect can enrich that context with references to the actual components in the codebase.

They solve related problems: MCP provides an interface for retrieving and using context; Code Connect establishes particular design-to-code mappings. Neither replaces the component's usage guidance or the application's business rules.

## Example: a booking action button

Suppose a team maps its Figma BookingButton to a shared code component. The mapping identifies the import and supported size and emphasis options. A working example shows a pending state.

The implementation task still needs to specify when a booking request starts, how repeat submission is handled, and what happens after a failure. These decisions belong in the product flow and relevant documentation.

Review the generated use of the component against its real API, then test the surrounding interaction.

## What should teams maintain?

Update mappings when component identities, imports, or supported properties change. Check representative design instances against the current released implementation. Give unresolved mappings a visible owner instead of treating them as successful connections.

Keep version and access details in the project's setup documentation. Treat the mapping as a maintained connection to implementation, and check the resulting behavior in the product.

## Related terms

- [Figma MCP Server](/glossary/figma-mcp-server.html)
- [Design-to-Code Workflow](/glossary/design-to-code-workflow.html)
- [Component Architecture](/glossary/component-architecture.html)
- [Design System Documentation](/glossary/design-system-documentation.html)

## Sources

- [Code Connect introduction, Figma](https://developers.figma.com/docs/code-connect/)
- [Getting started with Code Connect CLI, Figma](https://developers.figma.com/docs/code-connect/quickstart-guide/)

name: Figma MCP Server
definition: The Figma MCP server connects compatible AI tools to Figma through the Model Context Protocol. It provides tools for accessing design context and, in supported workflows, creating or modifying native Figma content.
contentMarkdown:
# Figma MCP Server

The Figma MCP server connects compatible AI tools to Figma through the Model Context Protocol. It provides tools for accessing design context and, in supported workflows, creating or modifying native Figma content.

## What can the Figma MCP server provide?

Figma's documented capabilities include retrieving component, variable, and layout context; using design-to-code mappings; and working with supported resources from design files. Some remote-server workflows also support writing to the canvas or bringing a browser interface into editable Figma layers.

Availability depends on the connection, client, permissions, and feature. The official documentation distinguishes remote and desktop servers. Follow its current setup and access guidance rather than assuming the two expose identical capabilities.

## Example: implementing a reservation card

A designer gives an agent the URL of a specific Figma selection and identifies the repository to use. The agent retrieves design context and checks for connected code components.

Before implementation, the task specifies the real data fields, loading state, and behavior for a canceled reservation. Afterward, the team reviews long names, missing values, keyboard interaction, and layout at a narrow width.

The Figma selection helps describe the intended interface. It does not supply every business rule or demonstrate that the generated implementation works.

## Figma MCP vs. Code Connect vs. a design system MCP

| Term | Main role |
|---|---|
| Model Context Protocol | A protocol through which a client interacts with tools and context |
| Figma MCP server | A Figma-specific integration exposing supported tools |
| Figma Code Connect | Mappings between design components and code implementations |
| Design system MCP | A descriptive label for an integration that exposes a system's components or guidance |

There is no single mandatory “design system MCP” product or content format. A [Storybook](/glossary/storybook.html) integration, for example, exposes different implementation context from a Figma integration.

## What context improves the result?

Give the agent a specific selection, the intended task, repository conventions, and references to existing components. State what it may change and the checks the result must pass. An instruction to reuse a component is useful only if the agent can find its supported API.

[Code Connect](/glossary/figma-code-connect.html) can make the mapping to actual code more explicit. Human review and appropriate tests still determine whether the output meets the requirements.

Use the official setup documentation for connection details. Choose the connection supported by your client, then confirm which tools it exposes before planning the workflow.

## Related terms

- [Model Context Protocol](/glossary/model-context-protocol-mcp.html)
- [Figma Code Connect](/glossary/figma-code-connect.html)
- [Design Harness](/glossary/design-harness.html)
- [Design-to-Code Workflow](/glossary/design-to-code-workflow.html)

- [Code-to-Design Workflow](/glossary/code-to-design-workflow.html)

## Sources

- [Figma MCP server introduction](https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/)
- [Code Connect introduction, Figma](https://developers.figma.com/docs/code-connect/)

name: Code-to-Design Workflow
definition: A code-to-design workflow brings an implemented interface into a design environment for inspection, discussion, or further exploration. It can capture rendered screens as editable design layers or connect code-based components to design work.
contentMarkdown:
# Code-to-Design Workflow

A code-to-design workflow brings an implemented interface into a design environment for inspection, discussion, or further exploration. It can capture rendered screens as editable design layers or connect code-based components to design work.

## When is code-to-design useful?

A product may have changed in code while design files remain behind. Capturing the current interface can help a team compare states, discuss a flow, or explore a revision using the implementation as a reference.

It can also help when an interactive prototype was built directly in code. The team can review its visible states together rather than treating an earlier design file as an exact record of the latest interface.

## Example: reviewing a quote-request flow

Suppose an AI-assisted prototype includes an initial form, validation errors, a loading state, and confirmation. The designer captures each important state and arranges them together for review.

The review identifies an unclear error message and a missing recovery route. The team records the changes, implements them in code, and checks the running flow again.

The captured screens support discussion. They do not replace testing the interaction, data handling, or accessibility of the working page.

## Does capture preserve the original components?

Not necessarily. A capture can reproduce visible layers without preserving the code's component boundaries, design-library instances, or business logic.

Figma's documented code-to-canvas workflow uses a supported client and the remote MCP server to capture live browser UI into editable Figma layers. The guide distinguishes capture from creating content with existing library components.

Check what a particular method preserves. Editable text or an associated variable does not establish a complete connection to the original component or source code.

## Code-to-design vs. design-to-code

[Design-to-code](/glossary/design-to-code-workflow.html) starts with a design representation and creates or updates implementation. Code-to-design starts with implementation and brings information back into design work.

A round trip may include both. It does not imply continuous, lossless, bidirectional synchronization. Teams still need to identify the authoritative implementation, the reviewed state, and how decisions become changes.

Capture representative states with safe test data, note the implementation version, and keep a route back to the running interface. A static visual reference is useful when its scope and age are clear.

## Related terms

- [Design-to-Code Workflow](/glossary/design-to-code-workflow.html)
- [Figma MCP Server](/glossary/figma-mcp-server.html)
- [Figma Code Connect](/glossary/figma-code-connect.html)
- [Design QA](/glossary/design-qa.html)

## Sources

- [Code to canvas, Figma](https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/code-to-canvas/)
- [Figma MCP server introduction](https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/)

name: Design System Adoption
definition: Design system adoption is the extent to which teams use and maintain a design system's shared components, guidance, and practices in their products. Adoption includes the ongoing work of integrating updates and using the system appropriately.
contentMarkdown:
# Design System Adoption

Design system adoption is the extent to which teams use and maintain a design system's shared components, guidance, and practices in their products. Adoption includes the ongoing work of integrating updates and using the system appropriately.

## What counts as adoption?

Define the behavior you want to understand before counting it.

| Signal | What it can establish |
|---|---|
| A package is installed | A project has a dependency |
| A component is imported | Code references that component |
| A component appears in a flow | The implementation is used in that context |
| A team updates and contributes | There is continuing participation |

These signals answer different questions. None alone proves that the resulting experience is usable or that the system meets the team's needs.

## Example: adoption across eight products

Suppose five of eight eligible products use the current shared form controls. Product-level adoption for that defined scope is 5 ÷ 8, or 62.5%.

That does not mean 62.5% of all fields use those controls. Component coverage needs a different denominator, such as the number of eligible field instances in inspected flows.

Record the eligibility rule, version, measurement method, and date. Treat a pilot using one component differently from a product that has migrated its main workflows.

## How do you improve adoption?

Start with a recurring need the system can meet. Work with a consuming team to integrate the relevant component into a real task. Observe where the API, guidance, access, or migration process creates friction.

Useful responses may include a working example, a clearer contribution route, compatibility support, or a missing component state. Avoid treating every exception as resistance: an unsupported need may justify an extension or a different solution.

USWDS provides an example of incremental adoption through principles, guidance, and code. A team does not have to replace every interface at once to begin using shared practices.

## Adoption vs. design system value

Adoption describes use. Value concerns what that use helps people and teams achieve.

Pair usage signals with outcomes such as fewer repeated implementation problems, easier maintenance, or better task performance. Record the baseline and other changes that might affect the result. More system usage is not automatically a better user experience.

Give teams a way to report gaps and receive updates. Sustainable adoption depends on a maintained relationship between system owners and product teams.

## Related terms

- [Design System Metrics](/glossary/design-system-metrics.html)
- [Component Telemetry](/glossary/component-telemetry.html)
- [Design System Governance](/glossary/design-system-governance.html)
- [Design System Migration](/glossary/design-system-migration.html)

## Sources

- [USWDS maturity model](https://designsystem.digital.gov/maturity-model/)
- [Community, GOV.UK Design System](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/community/)
